questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 7 AM and 8 AM will the hour and minute hands of the clock overlap?
questions.solution:
The formula for the angle between the hands is: Angle = |30H - {11 over 2}M|

Where **H** = hours and **M** = minutes.

Since the time is between **7 AM** and **8 AM**, we take **H = 7**.

For the hands to **overlap**, we set Angle = 0°:

0 = |30 × 7 − 5.5 × M|

0 = |210 − 5.5M|

5.5M = 210

M = 210 ÷ 5.5

M = 420 ÷ 11

M = 38 2/11 ≈ **38.18 minutes**

So, the time is approximately **7:38 AM**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **7:38**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 4**”.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the hour hand and minute hand = |60H - 11M| over 2

For an **overlap**, the angle is 0°.

Given **H = 7** (as the time is between 7 AM and 8 AM).

0 = |60 times 7 - 11 times M| over 2

0 = |420 − 11M|

11M = 420

M = 420 ÷ 11 = 38 2/11

M ≈ **38.18**

The time at which the hands overlap is approximately **7:38 AM**.

Hence, the correct answer is **7:38**.

questions.question: Which of the following groups of animals produce ultrasound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dolphins, bats, and porpoises**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ultrasound** is defined as sound waves with frequencies higher than the upper limit of human audibility, which is typically above **20,000 Hz** (20 kHz).
 
• **Bats** are well-known for producing ultrasonic squeaks. They use these high-frequency waves for **echolocation**, allowing them to navigate and hunt insects in total darkness by interpreting the echoes that bounce back from objects.
 
• **Dolphins** and **porpoises** produce ultrasonic clicks and whistles for underwater communication and **sonar**. These high-frequency sounds travel efficiently through water, helping them detect prey and obstacles with extreme precision.
 
• Certain other animals, such as **shrews** and some species of **moths**, also interact with ultrasound for survival, either by producing it for navigation or sensing it to avoid predators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classification of Sound Frequencies**:

 
 
• **Infrasound**: Sound waves with frequencies lower than **20 Hz**. These are produced by large animals like **elephants**, **rhinoceroses**, and **whales** (specifically baleen whales) to communicate over vast distances.
 
• **Audible Sound**: The frequency range that the human ear can perceive, spanning from **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**.
 
• **Ultrasound Applications**: In the medical field, **ultrasonography** uses high-frequency waves to visualize internal organs or fetal development. In industries, it is used for **ultrasonic cleaning** and detecting cracks in metal blocks.
 
 
 
• **Biological Variations**:
 
 
• While **dogs** can hear frequencies higher than humans (up to 45,000 Hz), they primarily communicate within the audible range and do not use ultrasound for navigation like bats or dolphins.
 
• **Moths** have developed the ability to hear the ultrasonic pulses of bats, which serves as an evolutionary defense mechanism to escape predation.

questions.question: A pencil partially dipped in water appears bent at the surface. Which phenomenon explains this?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Refraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Refraction** is the scientific phenomenon where light **changes direction** and **speed** as it passes from one transparent medium to another of different **optical density**.
 
• When a **pencil** is partially submerged in **water**, light rays reflecting from the underwater portion travel from water (an **optically denser medium**) into the air (an **optically rarer medium**).
 
• As these light rays cross the **interface** between water and air, they **speed up** and bend **away from the normal**.
 
• The human eye and brain trace these refracted rays back as **straight lines**, creating a **virtual image** of the pencil that appears at a shallower depth than its actual position.
 
• This displacement of the submerged part relative to the part in the air causes the pencil to appear **bent** or **broken** at the water surface.
 
• The degree of bending is determined by the **Refractive Index** of the materials, which for **water** is approximately **1.33** and for **air** is nearly **1.00**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reflection**

 
 
• Involves the **bouncing back** of light waves when they encounter a surface that does not absorb the energy.
 
• It follows the **Laws of Reflection**, where the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
 
 
 
• **Diffraction**
 
 
• Refers to the **bending of light** waves around the **edges** of an obstacle or through a narrow opening.
 
• It is most prominent when the size of the obstacle is comparable to the **wavelength** of the light.
 
 
 
• **Interference**
 
 
• Occurs when two or more light waves **superimpose** to form a resultant wave of greater, lower, or the same amplitude.
 
• This principle is responsible for the **iridescent colors** seen in thin films like soap bubbles or oil slicks.

questions.question: Which key fiscal reform was introduced in India after 1991 to strengthen revenue collection?

options.text: Introduction of Goods and Services Tax (GST)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Simplifying indirect taxes through MODVAT**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Following the **1991 Economic Reforms**, India focused on **fiscal consolidation** to stabilize the economy and address the balance of payments crisis.
 
• The **Tax Reforms Committee (1991)**, chaired by **Dr. Raja J. Chelliah**, recommended structural changes to the tax system to improve efficiency and **revenue collection**.
 
• A major component of these reforms was the simplification of **indirect taxes** through the expansion of **MODVAT (Modified Value Added Tax)**, which aimed to reduce the **cascading effect** of taxes (tax on tax).
 
• **MODVAT** allowed manufacturers to claim **input tax credit** for duties paid on raw materials and components, ensuring that tax was levied only on the **value added** at each stage of production.
 
• By streamlining the **excise duty** structure and reducing the multiplicity of rates, the government encouraged **tax compliance** and widened the tax base, leading to more robust revenue growth.
 
• Therefore, simplifying indirect taxes through MODVAT was a critical fiscal strategy introduced and expanded in the post-1991 era to strengthen the national treasury.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**:

 
 
• While it is a landmark reform, it was officially implemented much later on **July 1, 2017**, under the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act**.
 
• It integrated various indirect taxes like **Central Excise Duty**, **Service Tax**, and **State VAT** into a single unified tax.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Management Post-1991**:
 
 
• The government aimed to reduce the **fiscal deficit**, which had reached **8.4%** of GDP in **1990-91**.
 
• Reforms focused on **expenditure control**, meaning the policy was to rationalise or reduce **unproductive subsidies** rather than increase them.
 
• **Direct Tax Reforms** involved lowering **marginal tax rates** for individuals and corporations to discourage evasion and promote investment, rather than removing **income tax** entirely.

questions.question: What is a "slap shot" in hockey?

options.text: A shot taken with an open hand
A hard shot taken with a stick that is swung back and then quickly forward
A shot taken from a short distance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A hard shot taken with a stick that is swung back and then quickly forward**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **slap shot** is a high-velocity technique in **ice hockey** designed to maximize power and speed, often reaching velocities over **100 miles per hour** (160 km/h).
 
• The execution involves three distinct phases: a **backswing** where the stick is raised above the waist or shoulder, a rapid **downswing**, and a follow-through.
 
• Scientifically, the player does not aim directly for the puck but strikes the **ice surface** roughly 1-2 inches behind it, causing the stick to **flex** significantly.
 
• This **mechanical flexing** stores **elastic potential energy** within the stick shaft, which is then released like a spring as the blade makes contact with the puck, propelling it forward with extreme force.
 
• The **slap shot** is statistically the most powerful shot in hockey but is generally considered less accurate than other shooting techniques due to the long delivery time and high force involved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Comparison with other technical shots:
 
 
• **Wrist Shot**: Unlike the slap shot, this technique involves the puck staying in contact with the blade throughout the motion. It relies on a quick **snap of the wrists** to generate **accuracy** and a **deceptive release**, making it the most common shot in **NHL** gameplay.
 
• **Snap Shot**: Often described as a hybrid, it uses a shorter backswing than a slap shot but still utilizes **stick flex** for power. It is prized for its ability to be released while the player is in full stride.
 
• **Historical Background**: **Bernard 'Boom Boom' Geoffrion** of the **Montreal Canadiens** is widely credited with innovating and popularizing the slap shot in the 1950s, while **Bobby Hull** later became famous for its terrifying speed.
 
• **Equipment Evolution**: The transition from **wooden sticks** to **carbon fiber composites** has allowed players to customize the **flex rating** of their equipment, further enhancing the power generated during a slap shot.

questions.question: Who assisted Humayun in regaining the Mughal throne after his exile?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Persian ruler Shah Tahmasp**__.

• After years of wandering in **Sindh** and **Marwar**, **Humayun** sought political asylum in **Persia** at the court of the **Safavid** monarch, **Shah Tahmasp I**.
 
• **Shah Tahmasp** provided **Humayun** with a robust military force of approximately **12,000 cavalry** and **artillery** support to regain his lost territories.
 
• As a condition for this support, **Humayun** was required to adopt **Shia Islam** and agreed to cede the strategic territory of **Kandahar** to the **Persian** empire upon its conquest.
 
• With the backing of the **Safavid** army, **Humayun** first captured **Kandahar** and **Kabul** from his brother **Kamran Mirza** in **1545**, which eventually paved the way for his return to **Delhi** in **1555**.

• He is renowned for his administrative genius, including the introduction of the **Rupiya** and the restoration of the **Grand Trunk Road**.
 
 
 
• **Bahadur Shah of Gujarat**
 
 
• A powerful **Sultan** who expanded his kingdom into **Malwa** and **Rajasthan**.
 
• He was a constant threat to **Humayun** during the early **1530s** until his defeat and subsequent death in a conflict with the **Portuguese**.

questions.question: Where was India's first Export Processing Zone (EPZ) set up?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kandla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India was a pioneer in **Asia** by recognizing the effectiveness of the **Export Processing Zone (EPZ)** model, leading to the establishment of the continent's first EPZ in **Kandla** in **1965**.
 
• The **Kandla Export Processing Zone (KASEZ)** was set up in the state of **Gujarat** near the **Gulf of Kutch** to leverage its strategic coastal location for international trade.
 
• The primary objectives of establishing the **EPZ** were to boost **industrialization**, promote **export-oriented production**, earn **foreign exchange**, and generate **employment opportunities**.
 
• Following the success of the **Kandla** model, several other **EPZs** were established across India, including **Santacruz** (Maharashtra), **Cochin** (Kerala), **Chennai** (Tamil Nadu), and **Noida** (Uttar Pradesh).
 
• In **2000**, the Indian government introduced the **Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Policy** to address the shortcomings of the **EPZ** framework, such as bureaucratic hurdles and lack of world-class infrastructure.
 
• By **2005**, the **SEZ Act** was enacted, and all existing **EPZs**, including **Kandla**, were converted into **Special Economic Zones** to provide a more competitive and investor-friendly environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mundra:**

 
 
• Located in the **Kutch district** of **Gujarat**, it is home to **India's largest private port** and a massive **multi-product SEZ** operated by the **Adani Group**.
 
• While it is a major economic hub today, it was developed much later than the **Kandla EPZ**.
 
 
 
• **Paradip:**
 
 
• Situated at the confluence of the **Mahanadi River** and the **Bay of Bengal** in **Odisha**, it is one of India's major **natural deep-water ports**.
 
• It primarily handles the export of **iron ore** and **coal** but was not the site of the first **EPZ**.
 
 
 
• **Haldia:**
 
 
• Located at the mouth of the **Hooghly River** in **West Bengal**, **Haldia Port** was developed as a **satellite port** to the **Kolkata Port**.
 
• It serves as a major **petrochemical** and **industrial hub** for Eastern India.

• The **Mahila Aarogyam Kaksh** often functions in coordination with the **Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS)** or **AIIMS** to ensure professional medical assistance is available during court working hours.

questions.question: Article 32 of the Indian Constitution is related with which of the following?

• **Article 32** of the **Indian Constitution** provides the **Right to Constitutional Remedies**, which allows citizens to move the **Supreme Court** for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** guaranteed under **Part III**.
 
• Dr. **B.R. Ambedkar** described this article as the **'Heart and Soul of the Constitution'** because it makes the fundamental rights functional and enforceable.
 
• Under this article, the **Supreme Court** acts as the **guarantor** and **defender** of fundamental rights and has the power to issue directions or orders.
 
• The court can issue five types of **Prerogative Writs**: **Habeas Corpus**, **Mandamus**, **Prohibition**, **Certiorari**, and **Quo-Warranto**.
 
• This right cannot be suspended except as otherwise provided for by the **Constitution** (such as during a **National Emergency** under **Article 359**).
 
• The **Supreme Court** has ruled that **Article 32** is a **Basic Structure** of the Constitution, implying it cannot be removed even via a constitutional amendment.

• **Protection of interests of minorities**:
 
 
• This is covered under **Article 29**, which grants any section of citizens residing in India the right to conserve their distinct **language, script, or culture**.

• While **Article 32** gives powers to the **Supreme Court**, **Article 226** empowers **High Courts** to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.

• This article is a cornerstone of the **Separation of Powers** doctrine in India, designed to protect the **independence** and **sovereignty** of the legislative branch from judicial overreach.
 
• It ensures that the **House** remains the sole master of its own **internal proceedings**, facilitating the smooth functioning of democracy without constant legal interruptions.

• The performance is characterized by distinct movements like the **Aramandi** (half-squat position), intricate footwork, and a complex system of **Mudras** (hand gestures) used for storytelling.
 
• A traditional performance follows a specific sequence: **Alarippu** (invocation), **Jatiswaram** (pure dance), **Shabdam** (short compositions), **Varnam** (the centerpiece), **Padam** (expressive lyrics), and **Tillana** (concluding rhythmic piece).
 
• The dance is accompanied by **Carnatic music**, typically featuring instruments like the **Mridangam**, **Nadeswaram**, **Flute**, and **Cymbals** handled by the **Nattuvanar**.

• **Lingbu**: A traditional **flute** used by shepherds and in folk songs across the high-altitude plateaus.

questions.question: _____ can also be observed when a fine beam of light enters a room through a small hole.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tyndall effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tyndall effect** is defined as the phenomenon where a beam of light is scattered by **colloidal particles** or particles in a very fine suspension, making the path of the light visible to the observer.
 
• When a fine beam of light enters a dark room through a small hole, it is intercepted by **dust and smoke particles** suspended in the air. These particles scatter the incident light in various directions, which allows the trajectory of the beam to be clearly seen.
 
• The intensity of the scattered light depends on the **density of the particles** and the **frequency** of the incident light. Generally, shorter wavelengths (blue light) are scattered more strongly than longer wavelengths (red light).
 
• This effect can also be observed in nature when sunlight passes through the **canopy of a dense forest**. In this scenario, the **mist** contains tiny droplets of water that act as colloidal particles dispersed in the air, causing the light to scatter.
 
• The Tyndall effect is used to distinguish between a **true solution** and a **colloidal solution**, as true solutions do not scatter light because their particles are too small (usually less than 1 nanometer).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brownian movement**

 
 
• It describes the continuous, **random zig-zag motion** of microscopic particles suspended in a fluid (liquid or gas).
 
• This motion results from the constant **bombardment** of the particles by the fast-moving molecules of the surrounding medium.
 
 
 
• **Diffraction**
 
 
• It refers to the **bending of light waves** as they pass around the edge of an object or through a narrow aperture.
 
• This phenomenon is most prominent when the size of the obstacle or opening is comparable to the **wavelength** of the light.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion**
 
 
• It is the process where **white light** splits into its seven constituent colors (VIBGYOR) when it passes through a transparent medium like a **glass prism**.
 
• This occurs because different colors of light travel at different speeds through the medium, resulting in different degrees of **refraction**.

questions.question: What is the largest 4-digit number that is divisible by 88?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is divisible by **88** if it is divisible by both **8** and **11**.

Check the largest option **9988**: Divisible by 11 but not by 8 (988 ÷ 8 = 123.5).

Check the next largest option **9944**: Divisible by 8 (944 ÷ 8 = 118) and 11 ((9+4) − (9+4) = 0).

**∴ The correct answer is 9944.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Largest **4-digit number** = 9999; Divisor = 88.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b170bcb1225931143b84096c3ce1b95e417d17ff7b1168a9ed2ab1f9afc08b2.png] 

⇒ Divide the largest 4-digit number 9999 by 88 to find the **remainder**.

⇒ 9999 ÷ 88 = 113.625

⇒ Quotient = 113

⇒ 88 × 113 = 9944

⇒ Remainder = 9999 − 9944 = 55

⇒ Largest 4-digit number divisible by 88 = 9999 − 55 = 9944

**∴ The correct answer is 9944.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if its **last three digits** are divisible by 8 (e.g., in 9944, 944 ÷ 8 = 118).

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the **absolute difference** between the sum of digits at odd places and even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Composite Divisibility

For any number to be divisible by a composite number like 88, it must be divisible by its **co-prime factors** (8 and 11 in this case).

questions.question: What is the smallest number that is a multiple of 11, 13, 22 and 26?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Break the numbers into their **prime factors**: 11, 13, (2 × 11), and (2 × 13).

To find the **LCM**, take the highest power of each prime factor present: 2, 11, and 13.

Multiply them together: 2 × 11 × 13 = 286.

**∴ The correct answer is 286.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The numbers are **11**, **13**, **22**, and **26**.

**Formula Used:** **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** is the smallest number that is a multiple of all the given numbers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/46b88f6148aaa3dfee174d9cea470083611bfcb3270de4efcb226ca39e8c5992.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 11 = 11¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 13 = 13¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 22 = 2¹ × 11¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 26 = 2¹ × 13¹

⇒ **LCM** = (Highest power of 2) × (Highest power of 11) × (Highest power of 13)

⇒ **LCM** = 2¹ × 11¹ × 13¹

⇒ **LCM** = 2 × 143

⇒ **LCM** = 286

**∴ The correct answer is 286.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The **LCM** of two or more numbers is the smallest number (not zero) that is a multiple of all the numbers in the set.

Prime Factorization Method

This method involves expressing each number as a product of **prime numbers** and then taking the highest power of each prime factor present across all numbers.

Relationship with HCF

For any two positive integers 'a' and 'b', the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

questions.question: A, B and C start at the same time in the same direction to run around a circular stadium. A completes a round in 120 seconds, B in 180 seconds and C in 240 seconds. All of them start from the same point. After how many minutes will they again be together at the starting point?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find when they meet at the **starting point**, calculate the **LCM** of their individual times.

Times given are 120, 180, and 240 seconds.

LCM(120, 180, 240) = 720 seconds.

Convert seconds to minutes: 720 ÷ 60 = 12 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** = 120 seconds

Time taken by **B** = 180 seconds

Time taken by **C** = 240 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Meeting time at starting point = **LCM** of (TimeA, TimeB, TimeC)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2540ef6502749f12a308169cf93ec90141003749c682b8a962c4c9fb79574b6b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 180 = 2² × 3² × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 240 = 2⁴ × 3 × 5

⇒ LCM = Highest power of each prime factor = 2⁴ × 3² × 5¹

⇒ LCM = 16 × 9 × 5 = 720 seconds

⇒ Time in minutes = 720 ÷ 60

⇒ Time = 12 min

**∴ The correct answer is 12 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting at the Starting Point

The time when multiple objects meeting again at the starting point is always the **LCM** of the time taken by each to complete one full revolution.

Meeting for the First Time (Anywhere)

To find when they meet for the first time anywhere on the track, use **Relative Speed**. Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed (Difference in speeds for same direction, sum for opposite).

LCM Applications

Commonly used in problems involving **traffic lights** changing simultaneously, **bells** tolling together, or periodic events overlapping.

questions.question: There are 600 men in a group. They have food for 90 days. After 6 days, 300 men left the group. Remaining food will last for how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining food lasts **600 men** for (90 − 6) = **84 days**.

Since the number of men is halved (from 600 to 300), the time will double.

Required days = 84 × 2 = **168 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 168 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial group size (M₁) = **600 men**

Initial duration (D₁) = **90 days**

Time passed = **6 days**

Men remaining (M₂) = 600 − 300 = **300 men**

**Formula Used:**

Remaining Food = M₁ × (D₁ − days passed) = M₂ × D₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d42707675745c29e4290e7d4e8314b2e164b9d1132b82758e143a49364ecc3b.png] 

⇒ Remaining days for the original group = 90 − 6 = 84 days

⇒ Total **man-days** of food left = 600 × 84

⇒ This food is now consumed by 300 men for D₂ days

⇒ 600 × 84 = 300 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = (600 × 84) ÷ 300

⇒ D₂ = 2 × 84 = 168 days

**∴ The correct answer is 168 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation in Provisions

When the total amount of **food** is constant, the number of **men** and **days** vary inversely. If the number of men is reduced to half, the food will last twice as long.

General Chain Rule Formula

The core formula for such problems is M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂. In provision cases, the **work** (W) is the food stock consumed.

Man-Days Concept

One **man-day** is the amount of food one man eats in one day. Total food = Total men × Total days.

questions.question: A man covers 1/3 part of a distance at the speed of 10 km/hr. He covers the remaining distance at the speed of 15 km/hr. What is the average speed (in km/hr) for this journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Distance** = 30 units (LCM of 10 and 15, multiplied by the fraction denominator 3).

**First Part** (1/3 of 30) = 10 units at 10 km/hr → Time₁ = 10 ÷ 10 = 1 hour.

**Second Part** (Remaining 20 units) = 20 units at 15 km/hr → Time₂ = 20 ÷ 15 = 4/3 hours.

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 30 ÷ (1 + 4/3) = 30 ÷ (7/3) = 90/7 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 90/7 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed 1** (v₁) = 10 km/hr for 1/3 of the **distance**.

**Speed 2** (v₂) = 15 km/hr for the remaining 2/3 of the **distance**.

**Formula Used:**

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d6202d11e35b58556bd0c154626895d4053f9953aa1d39eac50e6150f83cbcc7.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **total distance** be D km.

⇒ Time taken for the first part (t₁) = (D/3) ÷ 10 = D/30 hours.

⇒ Time taken for the second part (t₂) = (2D/3) ÷ 15 = 2D/45 hours.

⇒ Total Time (T) = t₁ + t₂ = D/30 + 2D/45

⇒ T = (3D + 4D) ÷ 90 = 7D/90 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = D ÷ (7D/90)

⇒ Average Speed = 90/7 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 90/7 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If a body covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, then **Average Speed** = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a body travels for equal time intervals at speeds v₁ and v₂, then **Average Speed** = (v₁ + v₂) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the **same direction** at speeds u and v, relative speed = |u − v|. For **opposite directions**, relative speed = u + v.

questions.question: When an article is sold for a discount of 25 percent, then there is a profit 60 percent. If the marked price of article is Rs. 800, then what is the cost price?

Use the ratio method: **CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)**

CP : MP = (100 − 25) : (100 + 60) = 75 : 160 = 15 : 32

Given, 32 units = Rs. 800 ⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 25

Cost Price = 15 units = 15 × 25 = Rs. 375

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 375.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Marked Price (MP)** = Rs. 800, **Discount** = 25%, **Profit** = 60%

**Formula:** Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D%)/100 | CP = SP × 100 / (100 + P%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/830e70bcb694ea8609b0587e0a0b7af286e48919badc6eccb2fba0da0f1acc97.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 800 × (100 − 25)/100

⇒ SP = 800 × 75/100 = Rs. 600

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 600 × 100 / (100 + 60)

⇒ CP = 600 × 100/160 = 600 × 5/8

⇒ CP = 75 × 5 = Rs. 375

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 375.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP and MP

The direct formula linking Cost Price and Marked Price is: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Markup Percentage

Markup is the amount added to CP to reach MP. Markup % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is [a + b − (ab/100)]%.

questions.question: Total marked price of 500 articles is Rs. 400. 25 percent discount is given. What will be the selling price for 15000 such articles? (marked price of each article is same)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Marked Price** for 15,000 articles = 400 × (15,000 ÷ 500) = 400 × 30 = ₹12,000.

**Discount** = 25% ⇒ Ratio of **Marked Price** to **Selling Price** = 100 : 75 = 4 : 3.

Since 4 units = ₹12,000, then 1 unit = ₹3,000.

**Selling Price** (3 units) = 3 × 3,000 = ₹9,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price** (MP) of 500 **articles** = ₹400

**Discount** percentage = 25%

**Formula Used:**

**Selling Price** (SP) = **Marked Price** × (100 − **Discount**%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72693d4dde9336709a7fc7302aec27612ee6a5dab44e342da06dbb351eb363ef.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Marked Price** of 1 **article** = 400 ÷ 500 = ₹0.80

⇒ Total **Marked Price** for 15,000 **articles** = 15,000 × 0.80 = ₹12,000

⇒ **Selling Price** of 15,000 **articles** = 12,000 × (100 − 25) ÷ 100

⇒ **Selling Price** = 12,000 × 75 ÷ 100

⇒ **Selling Price** = 12,000 × 0.75 = ₹9,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between MP and SP

The **Selling Price** is derived by subtracting the **Discount** from the **Marked Price**: SP = MP − Discount.

Discount Percentage

**Discount** % = (Discount ÷ **Marked Price**) × 100. It is always calculated on the **Marked Price** unless stated otherwise.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁ and d₂ are given, the effective discount is d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
People expect the train to arrive on time.

options.text: It will expected that the train will arrive on time.
People are expected the train will arrive on time.
The train is expected to arrive on time.
The train was expected on time by people.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The train is expected to arrive on time.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The provided sentence is in the **Active Voice** and follows the standard syntax: **Subject** (People) + **Verb** (expect) + **Object** (the train) + **Infinitive Phrase** (to arrive on time).

• In the transition to **Passive Voice**, the **Object** of the active sentence (**the train**) must function as the **New Subject** of the passive sentence.

• The main verb **expect** is in the **Simple Present Tense**. According to English transformational grammar, the passive form for the simple present is **is/am/are + Past Participle (V3)**. Since **the train** is a **singular noun**, the auxiliary verb **is** is paired with the past participle **expected**.

• The **to-infinitive** (to arrive) remains in its active infinitive form because the expectation concerns the future action of the train itself. This is a common structure for verbs of **perception**, **calculation**, or **expectation**.

• The original subject **People** is a **General Agent**. In passive constructions, indefinite or general agents like **people**, **someone**, or **they** are typically omitted as the focus is placed entirely on the **action** or the **recipient**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Passive Voice**:

• The **Passive Voice** is used to emphasize the **action** (the expectation) and the **object** (the train) rather than the **subject** performing the action.

• It is widely utilized in **formal reporting**, **scientific writing**, and **news headlines** to maintain an objective tone.

• **Verbs of Opinion and Expectation**:

• Verbs such as **expect**, **believe**, **report**, **claim**, and **think** can be converted using two passive structures:

• **Personal Passive**: [Subject] + [Passive Verb] + [to-infinitive] (e.g., **The train is expected to arrive...**).

• **Impersonal Passive**: It + [Passive Verb] + [that-clause] (e.g., **It is expected that the train will arrive...**).

• **Tense Maintenance**:

• A fundamental rule of **voice conversion** is that the **tense** must remain constant. If the active verb is **Present Tense** (expect), the passive auxiliary must also be **Present** (is expected). Converting it to **was expected** (Past) or **will be expected** (Future) would fundamentally change the meaning of the original statement.

</ul

__

• The structure for **Past Continuous (Passive Interrogative)** is: **Was/Were + Object + being + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject?**

• To convert this into the **Active Voice**, the structure must follow: **Was/Were + Subject + Verb-ing + Object?**

• In the passive sentence, **the rare paintings** is the object, and **the gallery** is the agent (subject). Hence, **the gallery** becomes the **grammatical subject** in the active voice.

• Since **the gallery** is a **singular collective noun** in this context, it requires the auxiliary verb **Was** rather than 'Were' to maintain subject-verb agreement.

• The passive construction **being displayed** is converted back to the active present participle form **displaying**.

• Combining these elements, the correct active construction is 'Was the gallery displaying the rare paintings during the summer exhibition?'.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Tense Conversion Rules**:

• **Simple Past**: Active (Did + Subject + V1) vs. Passive (Was/Were + Object + V3). Option 1 uses 'Did', which changes the **continuous aspect** of the original sentence.

• **Past Continuous**: Active (Was/Were + Subject + V1-ing) vs. Passive (Was/Were + Object + being + V3). This is the specific rule applicable here.

• **Present Perfect**: Active (Has/Have + Subject + V3) vs. Passive (Has/Have + Object + been + V3). Option 4 uses 'Have', which incorrectly changes the **tense** from past to present.

• **Subject-Verb Agreement**:

• In Option 2, the use of **Were** with **the gallery** is a grammatical error because a singular subject must be paired with a singular verb in standard **English grammar**.
